shared_reference.selection: maximum minimum coherence on common selected-component support

limitations: Each pair has its own reference/secondary interval. Unequal baselines, moisture, scattering and processing can change coherence; differences are not isolated event effects.
The shared reference pixel maximizes minimum coherence; independent stability is not established.
No atmospheric, ionospheric or tidal correction, LOS/vertical displacement, phase integration, SBAS inversion or forecasting is performed.
Native common pixel centers are intersected exactly. Connected-component IDs are local to each pair and are never matched numerically across dates.
Ionosphere-filled flags remain explicit; lack of a fill flag alone is not correction validation.
Ionosphere input eligibility is not correction accuracy or stable-ground validation.
Filled flags, finite screens and positive reported uncertainty are different quality conditions; absence of a fill flag does not establish trustworthy correction.
All fractions name their denominator. No correction is applied and no phase is integrated or converted into a deformation estimate.
The maximum-minimum-coherence candidate is a proposed data-support location, not an independently stable reference.
No earthquake detection, earthquake attribution, vertical motion or forecasting is inferred from this audit.

evidence.radar_comparator: Target minus median of the prior measured dates

signature_policy.interpretation: Evidence states refer to measured signatures or the explicitly named optical claim.

regional_context.scope: Persistent inundation reported for Bajo San Jorge–La Mojana, including San Marcos municipality.

limitations: The regional bulletin provides municipality-scale context. The measurements cover a 640 m square.
The October 3 radar pass is available as context and is outside the three-pass baseline.
The optical result describes strict open-water transitions between two snapshots on the 40 m comparison grid.
Mixed water, inundation beneath vegetation, and changes between the snapshots remain unresolved.
Radar signatures describe where the backscatter met the selected thresholds. Flood probability is unavailable.
